52:1: God Almighty means by His saying and the Mount: and the mountain called the Mount: and the mountain called the Mount. I have explained the meaning of At-Tur with its evidence, and we have mentioned the disagreement of those who differed about it in the past, which I mean by repeating it in this place. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty, And the Mount, he said: The mountain in Syriac.
52:2: And his saying: And an inscribed book means: And a written book. And from this is the saying of Ru’bah: I and the verses, line by line. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And an inscribed book, he said: Scrolls. Bishr told us: He said: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, And an inscribed book. The inscribed is the written. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, inscribed, he said: written. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, inscribed, that he said: written.
52:3: And his saying, On spread parchment, means: On spread paper. His saying in is related to written and the meaning of the statement is: A book written and written on spread paper. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: On an unfurled scroll, which is the book. Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: On a scroll. He said: A scroll is a document.
52:4: And his saying, And the House of Worship, means: And the House that is frequented by the large number of its visitors, and it is a house, as mentioned, in the heavens opposite the Kaaba on Earth, and seventy thousand angels enter it every day and then they never return to it again. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’a, a man from his people, who said: The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “The Frequented House was raised to me, so I said: O Gabriel, what is this? He said: The Frequented House is entered every day by seventy thousand angels. When they leave it, they do not return to what they are responsible for.” Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Khalid bin Al-Harith told us: Khalid bin Al-Harith told us: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, on the authority of Malik bin Sa’sa’ah, a man from his people, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, that a man said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: What is Al-Bayt Al-Ma’mur? He said: It is a house in the sky called Ad-Dirah, and it is opposite the Kaaba, above it. Its sanctity in the sky is like the sanctity of the House on Earth. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day and they never return to it. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Samak Ibn Harb: I heard Khalid Ibn Ar`arah say: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, go out to Al-Rahaba and Ibn Al-Kawwa or someone else said to him: What is Al-Bayt Al-Ma`mur? He said: It is a house in the sixth heaven called Ad-Dhirah, which seventy thousand angels enter every day and never return to it. Abu Kurayb told us: Talq bin Ghatam told us, on the authority of Zaidah, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ali bin Rabi’ah, who said: Ibn Al-Kawwa asked Ali, may God be pleased with him, about the Frequented House. He said: It is a mosque in the heavens called Ad-Dhirah, which seventy thousand angels enter every day and never return to. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Anbasa, on the authority of Ubayd al-Maktab, on the authority of Abu al-Tayyib, who said: Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the Ma’mur House. He said: It is a house opposite the ancient Kaaba in heaven, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, following the pattern of their banners. It is called Ad-Dirah. Each seventy thousand of the angels enter it, and they never return to it again. Ibn Hamid told us: Bahram told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man asked him about the Ma’mur House. He said: It is a house in the sky called the shrine, meaning the House. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day and then they do not return to it. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the Frequented House, he said: It is a house opposite the Throne that is frequented by angels. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day and then they do not return to it. Abdullah bin Ahmed bin Shabwaih told us: Ali bin Al-Hassan told us: Hussein told us: Ikrimah was asked while I was sitting with him about the Ma’mur House. He said: It is a house in the sky opposite the Kaaba. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, and the frequented house, he said: It is a house in the sky called Ad-Dhirah. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada: And the Frequented House - it was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said one day to his companions: Do you know what the Frequented House is? They said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: It is a mosque in the heavens, beneath which is the Kaaba. If it were to fall, it would fall on it. Seventy thousand angels pray in it every day. If they leave it, they will not return to what they are doing. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the Frequented House, that they claim that seventy thousand angels from the tribe of Iblis, who are called the jinn, go to it every day. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And the Frequented House, he said: The House of God which is in heaven. And he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Indeed, the House of God in heaven is entered every day the sun rises by seventy thousand angels, and then they never return to it after that. Muhammad bin Marzouq told us: Hajjaj told us: Hammad told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “The Frequented House is in the seventh heaven. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day and then they do not return to it until the Hour comes.” Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Fazzaz told us: Musa ibn Ismail told us: Sulayman told us, on the authority of Thabit, on the authority of Anas, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “When the angel ascended with me to the seventh heaven, I reached a building and said to the angel: What is this? He said: This is a building that God built for the angels. Seventy thousand angels enter it every day, sanctifying and glorifying God, and they do not return to it.”
52:5: And his saying: And the raised ceiling means by the ceiling in this place: the sky, and he made it a ceiling because it is a sky for the earth like the sky of the house, which is its ceiling. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Hanad bin Al-Sarri told us: Abu Al-Ahwas told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, that a man said to Ali, may God be pleased with him: What is the raised ceiling? He said: The sky. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Khalid ibn Arara, on the authority of Ali, who said: The raised ceiling is the sky. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Samak bin Harb, on the authority of Khalid bin Arara, on the authority of Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: A man asked him about the raised ceiling, and he said: The sky. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us on the authority of Samak bin Harb: I heard Khalid bin Ar`arah say: I heard Ali say: And the raised ceiling means the sky. He said: And We have made the sky a protected ceiling, but they, from its signs, are turning away. Al-Anbiya’ 32 Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the raised ceiling: he said: the sky. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Aqatada. And the raised ceiling is the ceiling of the sky. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, and the raised ceiling,: the ceiling of the sky.
52:6: And his saying, and the sea that is set on fire. The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of the sea that is set on fire. Some of them said: the burning one, and they interpreted that as: and the sea that is set on fire and heated. Who said that? Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said to a Jewish man: Where is Hell? He said: The sea. He said: I see him as nothing but truthful. And the sea is set ablaze. “And when the seas are set ablaze.” al-Takwir 81:6, lightened. Ibn Hamid told us: Yaqub told us, on the authority of Hafs ibn Hamid, on the authority of Shammar ibn Atiyah, regarding his statement, and the sea set ablaze, he said: It is like a set ablaze oven. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And the burning sea means the ignited one. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And the sea set ablaze, he said: The kindled. And he recited the statement of God Almighty, And when the seas are set ablaze (al-Takwir 81:6). He said: It was kindled. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And when the seas are filled. He said: The filled. Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, and the filled sea, meaning the full one. Others said: Rather, the imprisoned one is the one whose water has gone. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And the sea set ablaze, he said: Its fire is when its water disappears and it is proud. Others said: The imprisoned is the detained. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, and the imprisoned sea, he said: imprisoned. The first of the sayings on this matter, in my opinion, is the correct one, which says: The full sea is the one whose water is gathered together. This is because the most common meaning of sea is ignition, as it is said: I lit the oven, meaning: I lit it, or filling, as described, as Labid said: They were in the middle of the secret show and a crack in the wall, adjacent to its pen As Al-Nimr bin Tulab Al-Alki said: If he wants, he can look up and see the spring and the clouds around it. Watered by the rains of summer and autumn, they will never be deprived. If this is the most common meaning of the word sajr and the sea is not lit today, and God Almighty has described it as being lit, then one of the two attributes, which is lit, is invalidated, then the other attribute that it has today, which is fullness, is valid, because it is full at all times. It was said: This burning sea that our Lord, the Blessed and Exalted, swore by is a sea in the sky under the Throne. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ismail bin Abi Khalid, on the authority of Abu Saleh, on the authority of Ali, And the sea of fire, he said: A sea in the sky under the throne. He said: Mihran told us. He said: I heard it from Ismail. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abdullah bin Amr: And the sea of fire. He said: A sea under the throne. Muhammad bin Amara told me: Ubaidullah bin Musa told us: Ismail bin Abi Khalid told us on the authority of Abu Saleh regarding his statement, And the sea that is set ablaze, he said: A sea under the throne.
52:7: And His saying, Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. God Almighty says to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. O Muhammad, it will befall those who disbelieve in Him on the Day of Resurrection. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. The oath occurred here: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass. That is on the Day of Resurrection. His saying, There is no one to avert it, means: There is no one to avert that punishment that will befall the disbelievers, to repel it from them and save them from it when it befalls them.
52:8: And his saying, There is no one to avert it, means: There is no one to avert that punishment that will befall the disbelievers, to repel it from them and save them from it when it befalls them.
52:9: God Almighty says: The punishment of your Lord will surely come to pass on the Day when the sky will shake violently. “Day” is from the root word waqi’, and by his saying shatter he means: it will spin and be toppled. Muammar ibn al-Muthanna used to recite the verse of al-A’sha: As if her walk from her neighbor's house was like a cloud, neither slowing down nor hurrying up. According to his narration: the swaying and sagging in the walk, but as for others, he used to narrate it as the passing of the cloud. The commentators differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said something similar to what we have said. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On the Day the sky will shake with a shaking, he said: He means: with movement. Ibn Al-Muthanna and Amr bin Malik told us: Abu Muawiyah Al-Dharee’ told us, on the authority of Sufyan bin Uyaynah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, On the Day the sky will shake with a shake, he said: The sky will shake with a shake. Al-Hasan bin Ali Al-Sada’i told us: Ibrahim bin Bashar told us: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us: They told me on the authority of Muawiyah Al-Dharee’, on the authority of me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: On the Day the sky will shake with a shake, he said: It will rotate in circles. Harun bin Hatim Al-Maqri told us: Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us: Abu Muawiyah told me, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: On the Day the sky will shake with a shake, he said: It will rotate in circles. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, On the Day the sky will shake with a shaking. “Shaking it” means moving it. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, The Day the heaven will shake with a shake, meaning: its rotation and movement by the command of God, and the waves of some parts of it against others. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan who said: Ad-Dahhak said, On the Day the sky will sway with a sway, meaning that some parts of it will sway against others and move by the command of God. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, On the Day the sky will shake with a shake, that this is the Day of Resurrection. As for the shake, we have no knowledge of it. Others said: its cracking. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, The Day the sky will sway with a sway, he said: The Day the sky will split.
52:10: And His saying, And the mountains will move, means: And the mountains will move from their places on the earth and will become scattered dust.
52:11: God Almighty says: The valley that flows with pus and blood in Hell on the Day when the sky will swell, and that is the Day of Resurrection for those who deny the occurrence of God for the unbelievers on the Day when the sky will swell, and some of the grammarians of Basra used to say: The letter fa was inserted in His statement So woe that Day because it means if such and such was, so it is similar to recompense, because the predicate of recompense is with the letter fa. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: All times are with the future, so this is from that because they likened in, which is the origin of recompense, to a time. He said: In with the day, there is an implied verb, even though the interpretation is recompense, because the syntax takes the apparent meaning of the speech, even though the meaning is recompense.
52:12: And His statement, Those who are engaged in idle talk, means: Those who are engaged in temptation and mingling in this world, playing, heedless of what they will come to of God’s punishment in the Hereafter.
52:13: And His statement, On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, a summoning, God Almighty says: So woe to the deniers on the Day they are summoned. His saying, On the Day they are called is a translation of his saying, On that Day and a substitution for it. What is meant by his saying, They are called is that they are pushed with exhaustion and disturbance. It is said from this: I pushed him in the back of his neck: if I pushed him in it. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me: Abu Kudayna told us, on the authority of Qabus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, summoned. He said: It will be pushed around their necks until they are brought to the Fire. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, summoned, meaning: they are pushed. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, driven forcefully, he said: They are pushed into it forcefully. Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Wadh told us: Al-Hussein told us, on the authority of Zaid, on the authority of Ikrimah: On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, a summons. He says, to the Fire of Hell, a push. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell with a summons, he said: They are driven to it with a summons. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada, something similar. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, a summons. “Submission” means pushing and exhaustion. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told me: Ibn Zayd said about the statement of God, On the Day they are summoned to the Fire of Hell, with a summons, he said: They are pushed with a summons. And he recited the statement of God, the Most High, That is he who drives away the orphan Al-Ma’un 2. He said: He pushes him away and is harsh with him.
52:14: And His statement: This is the fire which you used to deny. God Almighty says: It will be said to them: This is the fire which you used to deny in this world, so you denied that you would enter it or that your Lord would punish you with it, and leaving out mentioning it is said to them as a sufficiency of the speech’s indication of it.
52:15: God Almighty says, informing us of what will be said to these deniers, whose characteristics He described, when they enter Hell on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:Is this, O people, that which you have just entered, bewitched, or will you not see it or perceive it? This was said to them as a rebuke, not as a question.
52:16: And His statement, Enter it, means: Taste the heat of this fire which you used to deny, and return to it. Be patient with its pain and severity, or do not be patient with that. It is the same for you whether you are patient or not. You will only be recompensed for what you used to do, meaning: You will only be punished for your actions, meaning you will only be punished for your disobedience in this world and your disbelief.
52:17: God Almighty says: Indeed, those who fear God by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins will be in gardens: meaning in orchards and pleasures therein, and that is in the Hereafter.
52:18: And his saying fruitful means: They have a lot of fruit. This is similar to what the Arabs say about a man who has a lot of dates: a man of dates. Or he has a lot of milk, so it is said: he is a milkman, as Al-Hutay’ah said: You deceived me and claimed that you are the son of Tamer in the summer His statement, because of what their Lord has given them, means that they have abundant fruit because God has given them that. And their Lord has protected them from the punishment of Hellfire, meaning that their Lord has lifted from them the punishment with which He punished the people of Hellfire.
52:19: God Almighty says: Eat and drink. It will be said to these righteous people in the gardens: Eat, O people, of what your Lord has given you and drink from its drink at ease. You will not fear from what you eat and drink therein any harm or any harm for what you used to do in this world for God of deeds.
52:20: And his saying, reclining on couches arranged in rows, has been made into rows, and he left out his saying, on cushions, as the meaning of what was mentioned in the speech was sufficient for it. And His statement: And We will marry them to fair women with large, beautiful eyes. God Almighty says: And We will marry the males from among these righteous men to wives with fair women. A man says: Marry this individual offspring or the individual sandal to this individual, meaning: Make them a pair. We have explained the meaning of marriage previously in a way that makes it unnecessary to repeat it here. And hours is the plural of houra, which is the intense whiteness of the eyeball with the intense blackness of the pupil. I mentioned the differences of opinion among the people of interpretation regarding this, and I explained what is correct in our view with evidence that makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. The eye is the plural of ‘ayna’, which is a large eye in beauty and spaciousness.
52:21: The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: Its meaning is that those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, We will join their believing offspring with them in Paradise, even if they did not reach the levels of their fathers through their deeds, as an honor to their believing fathers. We will not deprive their believing fathers of any of the rewards for their deeds. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding this verse: And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith, he said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, raises up the offspring of the believers, even if they are below him in deeds, so that God may delight His eyes with them. Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, raises the offspring of the believer in his degree, even if they are below him in deeds, in order to make him happy with them. Then he recited: And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: God, the Blessed and Exalted, raises the offspring of the believer with him in his degree. Then he mentioned something similar, except that he read: “And their offspring followed them in faith. We joined their offspring with them.” Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Muhammad bin Bishr told us: Sufyan bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sama’ah, on the authority of Amr bin Murrah, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, something similar. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of `Amr Ibn Murrah, on the authority of Sa`id Ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that he said regarding this verse, And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, he said: The offspring of the believer will be raised up to him and will join him even if they are below him in deeds. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: And those who believed and We followed their offspring who attained faith with faith, We joined with them their young offspring who had not attained faith, and We did not deprive the fathers of anything of their work. Mention of who said: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told us: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring. He says: Those whose offspring attain faith and act in obedience to Me - We will join them to Paradise through their faith, and their young children - We will join them with them. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And those who believe and whose offspring follow them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, meaning: Whoever’s offspring attain faith and learn of My obedience, I will join them with their fathers in Paradise, and their young children will also be like that. Others said something similar to this statement, except that they made the ha’ and the mim in his statement We joined them from the mention of offspring, and the ha’ and the mim in his statement their offspring from the mention of those who. They said: The meaning of the statement is: And those who believed and their young offspring followed them, and We did not deprive the adults of anything of their work. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring, he said: Their children attained the deeds that they had done and followed them in them, and their offspring who had not attained the deeds followed them. So God, the Most High, said, And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds, he said: He says: We did not wrong them in anything of their deeds, so that We would diminish them and give to them their offspring whom We joined with those who had not attained the deeds. We joined them with those who had attained the deeds. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is, Those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith, We will join their offspring with them. So We admitted them into Paradise because of the deeds of their fathers, and We did not deprive the fathers of anything of their deeds. Who said that? Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Al-Mu’tamir ibn Sulayman told us: I heard Dawud narrating on the authority of Aamir that he said regarding this verse: And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith - We will join with them their offspring and not deprive them of anything of their deeds. So God brought the offspring into Paradise because of the deeds of their fathers and did not deprive the fathers of anything of their deeds. He said: So this is His saying: And not deprived them of anything of their deeds. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, that he said regarding the statement of God, We joined their offspring to them, and We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds, that God joined their offspring to their fathers, and He did not diminish the fathers’ deeds by returning them to their children. Others said: What he meant by his saying, We joined their offspring to them, is that we gave them the same reward as we gave our fathers. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us on the authority of Qais ibn Muslim: I heard Ibrahim say regarding his statement, “And their offspring followed them in faith. We will join their offspring with them.” He said: They were given the same rewards as their fathers, and nothing was diminished from their rewards. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Qais bin Muslim, on the authority of Ibrahim: “And their offspring followed them in faith. We joined their offspring with them.” He said: They were given the same rewards as they were, and their rewards were not diminished. He said: Hakam told us on the authority of Abu Ja`far on the authority of al-Rabi`, And their offspring followed them in faith, meaning: We gave them the reward that We gave them, and We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds, meaning: We did not deprive their fathers of anything. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And those who believed and whose offspring followed them, Yazid said it this way, their offspring, “through faith, We will join their offspring with them,” he said: They acted in obedience to God, so God joined them with their fathers. The most correct of these sayings and the most similar to what is indicated by the apparent meaning of the revelation is the saying that we mentioned on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair on the authority of Ibn Abbas, which is: “And those who believed in God and His Messenger and We followed them with their offspring who attained faith with faith and believed in God and His Messenger - We will join with those who believed, their offspring who attained faith and believed in Paradise, and We will make them with them in their degrees, even though their deeds fell short of their deeds, as an honor from Us to their fathers. And We will not deprive them of anything of the reward of their deeds.” I said: This is the most appropriate interpretation of it because this is the most common of its meanings, even though there are other opinions. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, “And their offspring followed them in faith. We joined their offspring to them.” The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as, And their offspring followed them in faith, in the singular, We joined their offspring to them, in the plural. The reciters of Kufa read it as, “And their offspring followed them in faith. We joined their offspring to them,” both in the singular. Some of the reciters of Basra, namely Abu Amr, read, “And their offspring followed them in faith. We joined their offspring to them.” The correct thing to say about this is that all of these are well-known readings that are widespread in the readings of the regions and have similar meanings, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement, And We did not deprive them of anything of their work, God Almighty says: And We did not deprive the fathers, meaning by His statement, And We did not deprive them, and We did not reduce anything from the rewards of their work, so that we would take it from them and give it to their children whom We joined with them, but We paid them the rewards of their work and joined their children to their degrees, as a favor from Us to them. And alat in the speech of the Arabs means: deficiency and reduction, and there is another language for it, and no one reads it with it, We do it. And from alat is the saying of the poet: Tell Bani Tha'al on my behalf the most comprehensive message, neither by flattery nor by lies. Meaning: No decrease and no increase. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Muammil told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Murrah, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds. He said: We did not diminish them. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement: And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds, meaning: We did not diminish them. Musa bin Abdul Rahman told me: Musa bin Bishr told us: Sufyan bin Saeed told us, on the authority of Sama’ah, on the authority of Amr bin Marra, on the authority of Saeed bin Jubair, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds. He said: And We did not diminish them. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds. He said: We did not deprive the fathers of anything for the sons. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: We did not diminish the fathers for the sons, nor did we deprive them. He said: We did not diminish them. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds, he said: We diminished them. Ibn Hamid told us: Hakam told us, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Al-Rabi` bin Anas, And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds, meaning: We did not decrease anything from their deeds. He said: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Jaafar on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, similarly. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Mu`alla, on the authority of Sa`id Ibn Jubayr: And We did not deprive them. He said: And We did not wrong them. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And We did not deprive them of anything of their work, meaning: We did not wrong them anything of their knowledge. Muhammad bin Abdul A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada: And We did not deprive them of anything of their deeds. He said: And We did not wrong them. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And We did not deprive them, meaning: We did not wrong them. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And We did not deprive them of anything of their work, he said: He says: We did not wrong them in any of their work. We did not deprive them of anything, so that we would give them their offspring whom We joined with them who had not yet attained the work. He joined them with those who had attained the work. And We did not deprive them of anything of their work, he said: He did not take the work of the adults so that He would reward the children, and He admitted them with His mercy, and the adults worked, so they entered with their work. His saying, Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned, means: Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned and done of good and evil. No one will be held accountable for the sin of another, but rather he will be punished for his own sin.
52:22: God Almighty says: And We provided those who believed in God and His Messenger and whose offspring followed them in faith in Paradise with fruits and meat of whatever they desired of meat.
52:23: And his saying, They will compete over a cup therein, means: They will share a cup of drink therein and pass it around among themselves, as Al-Akhtal said: I quarreled with him for the sweet scent of the comprehensive wine, and the chickens crowed and the time came for the journey His saying, There is no idle talk in it, means: There is no falsehood in Paradise. The ha in his saying, in it, is from the mention of the cup, and the meaning is for what is in it of drink, meaning: that its people do not engage in idle talk in it, nor do they sin. And idle talk means falsehood. His saying, and no sin means: There is no action in it that would make its doer sinful. It was said that what is meant by sin is lying. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, There is no falsehood in it, meaning: There is no falsehood in it. And his saying, and no sin, means: no lie. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, There is no idle talk therein, he said: They do not insult each other. Nor sin, he said: Nor are they sinful. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, There is no idle talk in it nor sin: meaning there is no idle talk in it nor falsehood. Falsehood in this world was only with Satan. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Muhammad ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, There is no idle talk therein nor sin, he said: There is no idle talk or falsehood in it. Rather, the idle talk and falsehood were in this world. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement, There is no idle talk in it nor sin. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Kufa recited it, There is no idle talk in it nor sin, in the nominative case and with the tanween, as a statement that there is no idle talk or sin in the cup. Some of the reciters of Basra recited it, There is no idle talk in it nor sin, in the accusative case without the tanween, as a statement of exoneration. In my opinion, they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct, even though the raising and tanween readings are more pleasing to me because they are frequently recited and because they have the more correct meanings.
52:24: God Almighty says: And there will circulate among these people whose description He has described in Paradise, young boys of theirs, as if they were pearls in their whiteness and their qualities, hidden, meaning: protected in a hidden place, so it is purer for them and clearer in its whiteness. What He meant by that is that these young boys will circulate among these believers in Paradise with cups of drink whose description He, the Most High, has described. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And there will circulate among them young boys as if they were hidden pearls. He mentioned to us that a man said, O Prophet of God, this is the servant, but what about the master? He said, By the One in Whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, the superiority of the master over the servant is like the superiority of the moon on the night of the full moon over all the other stars. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, As if they were hidden pearls, he said: It reached me that it was said: O Messenger of God, this servant is like a pearl, so what about the one who is served? He said: By the One in Whose hand is my soul, the difference between them is like the difference between the moon on the night of the full moon over the stars.
52:25: And His saying, And some of them will turn to others... the verse says, the Almighty said: And some of these believers in Paradise will turn to others, asking each other. And it has been said that this will happen to them when they are resurrected from their graves. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And some of them will turn to others, asking questions, he said: When they are resurrected at the second blast.
52:26: God Almighty says: Some of them said to each other: O people, we were among our families in this world, fearful and apprehensive of God’s punishment, and apprehensive that our Lord would punish us today.
52:27: So God bestowed His favor upon us by His grace and saved us from the torment of the poisonous winds meaning: the torment of the fire meaning a cup of fire and brought us into Paradise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: K said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, The torment of the scorching wind, he said: The torment of the Fire.
52:28: And His statement, Indeed, we used to call upon Him before means: Indeed, we used to call upon Him in this world before this day, worshipping Him, devoting our religion to Him alone, not associating anything with Him. Indeed, He is the Most Kind meaning: The Most Kind to His servants. As Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Indeed, He is the Most Just, meaning: the Most Kind. And his saying, The Most Merciful, means: The Most Merciful to His creation does not punish them after their repentance. The reciters differed regarding his saying, Indeed, He is the righteous. The majority of the reciters of Medina read it as that He with a fat-ha on the alif, meaning: We used to call upon Him before because He is the righteous or because He is the righteous. The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra read it with a kasra as an initial. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings, so whichever one the reader recites, he is correct.
52:29: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So remind, O Muhammad, of those to whom you have been sent from your people and others, and admonish them with God’s blessings upon them. For you are not, by the grace of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman. He says, “So, by the grace of God upon you, you are not a soothsayer who prophesies, nor a madman who has a vision that he tells his people about which he did not tell them. Rather, you are the Messenger of God, and God will not let you down, but rather He will support you.”
52:30: And His statement, Or do they say, ‘He is a poet for whom we are waiting for a misfortune of time?’ God Almighty says: Rather, the polytheists say to you, O Muhammad: He is a poet for whom we are waiting for the misfortunes of time. We will suffice him with death or a devastating incident. And in a similar manner to what we have said about this, the people of interpretation said, although their expressions differed about it. Some of them said about it what we have said, and some of them said: It is death. It was mentioned that he said about me: The vicissitudes of fate: the accidents of time. Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, The vicissitudes of fate, he said: The events of time. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Sufyan, who said: Mujahid said: The vicissitudes of fate are the events of time. Mention of the one who said: It means death. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, the vicissitudes of fate, meaning death. Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, We are waiting for him to be struck by misfortune. He said: They are waiting for him to die. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Or do they say, ‘A poet for whom we are awaiting a misfortune of time?’ He said: Some people said that: Await death for Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it will suffice you against him, just as the poet of the Banu so-and-so and the poet of the Banu so-and-so sufficed you against him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us on the authority of Muammar on the authority of Qatada regarding his statement, The uncertainty of fate, he said: It is death. We wait for death just as the poet of the Banu so-and-so and the poet of the Banu so-and-so died. Saeed bin Yahya Al-Umawi told me: My father told me: Muhammad bin Ishaq told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that when the Quraysh gathered in the House of Assembly concerning the matter of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, one of them said: “Keep him in chains and await death for him until the poets before him, Zuhayr and An-Nabigha, perish. He is like one of them.” So God revealed concerning that from their saying: Or do they say, ‘He is a poet; we await for him a misfortune of death’? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, We await for him the vicissitudes of fate, death. And the poet said: The vicissitudes of fate lie in wait for her, perhaps her husband will perish or she will be set free. Others said: The meaning of this is: the turmoil of this world. They said: Al-Manun means death. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us on the authority of Abu Sinan: The vicissitudes of fate. He said: The vicissitudes of this world and fate: death.
52:31: And His statement, Say, ‘Wait,’ God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Say, O Muhammad, to these polytheists who say to you, ‘You are a poet, we are waiting for you to be struck by the vicissitudes of fate. Wait,’ meaning, wait and be patient in the vicissitudes of fate, for I am with you among those who are waiting for you until God’s command comes to pass concerning you.
52:32: God Almighty says: Do the dreams of these polytheists command them to say about Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: He is a poet and that what he brought is poetry? Or are they a transgressing people? God Almighty says: Their dreams and minds do not command them to do that. Rather, they are a transgressing people. They have transgressed against their Lord and have exceeded what He permitted and commanded them to do, of belief, to disbelief in Him. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Or do their dreams command them to do this? In the Age of Ignorance, they were considered people of dreams. So God said, Or do their dreams command them to do this? That they should worship idols while being mute and deaf and abandon the worship of God. So their dreams did not benefit them when they were for their worldly life and their minds were not for their religion. Their dreams did not benefit them. Some of the people of knowledge of the Arabic language from the people of Basra interpreted His statement, Or do their dreams command them, as meaning, they command them. And similar to what we said in the interpretation of His statement, Or are they a transgressing people? the people of interpretation also said. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Uthman ibn al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Or are they a transgressing people? He said: Rather, they are a transgressing people. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Uthman bin Al-Aswad, on the authority of Mujahid: Or are they a transgressing people? He said: Rather, they are a transgressing people.
52:33: And His statement, Or do they say, ‘You say it,’ God Almighty says: Or do these polytheists say, ‘Muhammad says, This is the Qur’an and you create it. And His saying, Rather, they do not believe, God Almighty says: They lied in what they said about that. Rather, they do not believe and acknowledge the truth that came to them from their Lord.
52:34: And His statement, Then let them produce a hadith like it, means, may His praise be glorified: So let those who say that to him from among the polytheists produce a Qur’an like it, for they are from the people of the language of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and it will not be difficult for them to produce something like what Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought, if they are truthful in that Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, says it and creates it.
52:35: God Almighty says: Were these polytheists created for nothing? That is, without fathers or mothers, they are like inanimate objects that do not reason or understand God’s argument, nor do they consider His warnings or learn from His admonitions. It has been said that the meaning of this is: Or were they created for nothing? Like someone saying: I did such and such for nothing, meaning: for nothing.
52:36: And His statement, Or are they the creators? He says: Or are they the creators of this creation? So they do not obey the command of God nor desist from what He has forbidden them from, because the Creator has the power to command and forbid. Or did they create the heavens and the earth? He says: Did they create the heavens and the earth, so they are the creators? But the meaning of that is: They did not create the heavens and the earth. Rather, they are not certain. He says: They did not refrain from obeying the command of their Lord and desisting from obeying Him in what He has commanded and forbidden, because they created the heavens and the earth, and so they were thereby lords. But they did so because they are not certain of God’s threat and what He has prepared for the people of disbelief in Him of punishment in the Hereafter.
52:37: God Almighty says: Do these deniers of God’s signs have the treasures of your Lord, O Muhammad? So, because of their self-sufficiency in that, they turn away from the signs of their Lord, or are they the ones in control? The commentators differed in their interpretation of this. Some of them said: It means, Or are they the ones who have power? Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Or are they the ones who control it? He said: The ones who have power. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Or are they the ones who are sent down? Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Or do they have the treasures of your Lord, or are they the controllers? He said: He says, Or are they the ones who are sent down? Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is: Or are they the masters? Among those who said this is Muammar ibn al-Muthanna, who said: It is said: You controlled me, meaning you took me as your servant. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of this is: Or are they the tyrants who are arrogant and haughty towards God? This is because the word dominant in the speech of the Arabs means the tyrant who is dominant, and from this is the saying of God, You have no control over them (al-Ghashiyah 88:22), meaning: I am not a tyrant who has power over them.
52:38: And his statement, Or do they have a ladder by which they listen? He says: Or do they have a ladder by which they ascend to the heavens, by which they listen to the revelation and claim that they heard there from God that what they are upon is true, so that they are adhering to what they are upon. And his saying: Then let their listener produce clear proof, meaning: If they claim that, then let someone produce who claims that he heard that and listened to it produce clear proof, meaning with an argument that shows that it is true, just as Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, produced it based on the truth of his words and his truthfulness in what he brought them from God. And peace in the speech of the Arabs means: the cause and the ladder. From this is the saying of Ibn Muqbil: A person does not acquire the most beautiful lands, nor build ladders for himself in the heavens. And from it is his saying: I made so-and-so a means for my need: if I made him a reason for it.
52:39: God Almighty says to the polytheists of Quraysh 106:O people, does your Lord have daughters and you have sons? That is an unfair division.
52:40: Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with a heavy debt? God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do you ask these polytheists to whom We sent you, O Muhammad, about what you are calling them to of the Oneness of God and His obedience, for a reward and compensation from their wealth, so that they are burdened with a heavy debt and are unable to respond to you in what you are calling them to. And in a similar manner to what we said about that, the people of interpretation said: Who said that? Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with debt? He said: Did you ask these people for a reward for their efforts, so that they are unable to accept Islam? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, Or do you ask them for a reward, so that they are burdened with a debt? He said: He says: I asked them for this a reward, so they were burdened with what he sought to take from them.
52:41: And His statement, Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down? God Almighty says: Or do they have knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down for the people, informing them of whatever they wish and telling them what they want.
52:42: God Almighty says: Rather, these polytheists, O Muhammad, want to plot against you and against the religion of God. Those who disbelieve are the ones who will be plotted against. He says: They are the ones who are plotted against instead of you, so trust in God and carry on with what He has commanded you to do.
52:43: And His statement, Or do they have a god other than God? God Almighty says: Or do they have a god who deserves to be worshipped other than God, so that it is permissible for them to worship him? He says: They have no god other than God, to whom all of His creation is due worship. Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. He says: To sanctify God from their association with Him and their worship of anyone other than Him.
52:44: God Almighty says: And if these polytheists see pieces of the sky falling, then a piece of it will fall. And... And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, an eclipse, meaning: cutting off. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And if they see a fragment, meaning: And if they see pieces from the sky falling, they say, ‘This is a heaped-up cloud.’ God Almighty says: They say about that fragment falling from the sky: This is a heaped-up cloud. He means by His statement, heaped-up, some of it on top of others. Rather, what He, the Most High, meant by this was the polytheists of Quraysh who asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, for signs and said to him: We will not believe in you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth (al-Isra’ 17:90) until His saying: and a fragment upon us (al-Isra’ 17:92). So God said to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And if these polytheists were to see what they asked for of signs and see a fragment of the sky falling, they would not change their disbelief and would say, This is only clouds, one above the other, because God has decreed that they will not believe. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, They say, ‘Heaped clouds.’ He said: They do not believe in a hadith nor do they have faith in a verse. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And if they see a fragment of the sky falling, they say, ‘It is clouds piled up.’ He said: When they asked about the fragment, they said, Let a fragment of the sky fall upon us, if you should be of the truthful. He said: He says, If we had done that, they would have said, ‘It is clouds piled up.’
52:45: And His statement, So leave them until they meet their Day on which they will be struck dead, God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: So leave these polytheists, O Muhammad, until they meet their Day on which they will be destroyed, and that will be at the first trumpet blast. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, In it they will be struck dumb. The majority of reciters of the regions, except for Asim, recited it with a fat-ha on the ya’ from yasaqun. Asim recited it yasaqun with a damma on the ya’ and the fat-ha. The two recitations are more pleasing to us because it is the more eloquent and well-known of the two languages, even though the other is permissible. This is because the Arabs say: the man was struck dumb and was struck dumb, and Sa’d and Sa’d. We have explained the meaning of the stunned with its evidence and what the people of interpretation said about it previously, so there is no need to repeat it.
52:46: He, the Most High, means by His statement, The Day their plot will not avail them at all, the Day of Resurrection until they meet their day on which they will be struck dead. Then He explained which day that day is, saying: The Day their plot will not avail them at all, meaning: their plotting will not ward off anything from God’s punishment from them. So the second day is a translation of the first. His saying, Nor will they be helped: Nor will anyone help them, so that they can take revenge on those who tortured and punished them.
52:47: And His statement, And indeed, for those who do wrong is a punishment less than that. The people of interpretation differed regarding the punishment that God threatened these wrongdoers with other than the Day of the Shock. Some of them said: It is the punishment of the grave. Who said that? Ismail bin Musa Al-Fazari told us: Sharik told us on the authority of Abu Ishaq on the authority of Al-Baraa: A punishment less than that. He said: The punishment of the grave. Ali told me: Abu Saleh told us: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, And indeed, for those who do wrong is a punishment less than that, meaning: the punishment of the grave before the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada that Ibn Abbas used to say: The punishment of the grave is in the Book of God: And indeed, for those who do wrong is a punishment less than that. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, that Ibn Abbas used to say: The punishment of the grave is in the Qur’an. Then he recited: And indeed, for those who do wrong is a punishment less than that. Others said: He meant hunger. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me: Al-Hasan told us: Warqa’ told us, both on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, A punishment less than that, he said: hunger. Others said: What he meant by that is: the calamities that befall them in this world, such as the loss of money and children. Who said that? Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And indeed, for those who have wronged is a punishment less than that, he said: Less than the Hereafter in this world with which He will punish them of the loss of wealth and children. He said: So for the believers, it is a reward and recompense from God, in addition to their misfortunes and the misfortunes of these people, which God hastened for them in this world. And he recited, So let not their wealth or their children impress you At-Tawbah 9:55 to the end of the verse. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that God, the Most High, mentioned that for those who wronged themselves by their disbelief in Him, there is a punishment other than the Day on which they will be struck dead, and that is the Day of Resurrection. So the punishment of the grave is other than the Day of Resurrection because it is in the Barzakh. And the hunger that befell the disbelievers of Quraysh and the calamities that befell them in their persons, wealth and children are other than the Day of Resurrection. And God did not specify a type of that for them other than the Day of Resurrection, rather He said, And indeed, for those who wronged is a punishment other than that. So all of that is a punishment for them, and that is other than the Day of Resurrection. So the interpretation of the statement is: And indeed, for those who disbelieved in God, there is a punishment from God other than the Day of Resurrection. But most of them do not know that they will taste that punishment.
52:48: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, And be patient over the decision of your Lord, O Muhammad, which He has decided upon you, and carry out His commands and prohibitions and convey His messages. For you are under Our eyes, God Almighty says: For you are under Our sight, We see you and We see your deeds, and We surround you and protect you, so that none of the polytheists who wish you harm will reach you. And His saying: And glorify the praises of your Lord. The people of interpretation differed in the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: If you get up from your sleep, say: Glory be to God and His praise. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us: Abu Ahmad told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas, regarding his statement, And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise, he said: From every dream, when he wants to rise, he says: Glory be to You and praise be to You. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abu Al-Ahwas Aouf bin Malik: And glorify the praises of your Lord. He said: Glory be to God and His praise. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise, he said: When he rises for prayer during the night or day and recites, O you who have believed, when you rise to prayer (al-Ma’idah 5:6). He said: From sleep. He mentioned it on the authority of his father. Some of them said: Rather, the meaning of this is: If you stand up for the obligatory prayer, say: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Juwaybir, on the authority of al-Dahhak: And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise. He said: When he stands up for prayer, he says: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, and blessed be Your name, and there is no god but You. And it was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise for the obligatory prayer. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is the opinion of the one who said: The meaning of this is to pray with praise to your Lord when you wake up from your sleep, and that is the sleep of the afternoon prayer, and what I meant was the noon prayer. I said: This statement is the more correct of the two statements because everyone agrees that it is not obligatory to say in prayer: Glory be to You and praise be to You, and what was narrated from Ad-Dahhak when standing up for prayer. So if the statement were as Ad-Dahhak said, then it would have been obligatory to say it, because His statement, And glorify the praises of your Lord, is a command from God Almighty to glorify Him. And in the consensus of everyone that it is not obligatory, there is clear evidence that the statement about that is not what Ad-Dahhak said. If someone says: Perhaps what is meant by it is exhortation and guidance, it is said: There is no evidence in the verse for that, and no proof has been established that what Al-Dahhak said is meant by that. So the consensus of all that glorifying God when standing up for prayer is something that Muslims have the choice to do is evidence for us that what is meant by it is exhortation and guidance. We said: He meant getting up from the midday nap because there is no obligatory prayer after a time of the well-known times of people’s sleep except after the night’s sleep, which is the dawn prayer, or after the midday nap, which is the noon prayer. So when he commanded, after His saying, And glorify the praises of your Lord when you rise, to glorify God after the stars have set, which is the two rak’ahs of dawn after people have risen from their night’s sleep, it is known that the command to glorify God after getting up from sleep is a command to the prayer that is obligatory after getting up from the midday nap, as we mentioned, not getting up from the night’s sleep.
52:49: And His saying: And during part of the night glorify Him means: And during part of the night glorify your Lord, O Muhammad, with prayer and worship, and that is the sunset prayer. Ibn Zayd used to say about this: Yunus told me that Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said about His statement, And during part of the night glorify Him, he said: And during part of the night is the evening prayer. And at the setting of the stars, meaning when the stars set at the beginning of the day. It was said: He meant the two rak'ahs of Fajr. Some of those who said that said: Muhammad bin Saad told me: My father told me: My uncle told me: My father told me on the authority of his father on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, So glorify Him and at the setting of the stars. He said: They are the two prostrations before the dawn prayer. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And during part of the night glorify Him and at the setting of the stars. We used to say that they are the two rak’ahs at the break of dawn. He said: It was mentioned to us that Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, used to say: They are dearer to me than red camels. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Zarara bin Awfa, on the authority of Saeed bin Hisham, on the authority of Aisha, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said about the two rak’ahs of dawn prayer: They are better than the entire world. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, And the setting of the stars. He said: Two rak’ahs before the dawn prayer. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday and Hammad bin Mas`adah told us: Hamid told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Ali, regarding his statement, And the setting of the stars, he said: The two rak`ahs, it was said, the dawn prayer. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us on the authority of Ata’ who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: And the setting of the stars means the two rak’ahs before dawn. Others said: What is meant by glorification is the setting of the stars in the obligatory dawn prayer. Who said that? It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubaid told us: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And the setting of the stars, that he said: The dawn prayer. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And the setting of the stars, he said: The dawn prayer. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: What is meant by it is the obligatory prayer, the dawn prayer. This is because God commanded, saying: And during part of the night glorify Him and at the decline of the stars. The two rak’ahs before the obligatory prayer are not obligatory, and no proof has been established that must be accepted that His saying glorify Him is recommended. We have demonstrated in more than one place in our book that God’s command is obligatory until proof is established that what is meant by it is recommended or not obligatory, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place.
